inspiration.observed_pattern: A CTE assigns ascending and descending ROW_NUMBER values to ordered measurements, then an aggregate over the central rank slice calculates a median.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independent service-queue duration report. Each queue ranks fixed ticket durations in both directions with deterministic ticket tie-breakers; a grouped outer query averages rows whose opposing ranks differ by at most one, covering odd and even queue sizes. The schema, values, aliases, and operational meaning are new.

fixture_notes: The minimized queue has four durations so the two central rows are both selected and averaged, retaining the even-cardinality median boundary.
determinism_notes: Queue name, ticket IDs, durations, ascending and descending rank tie-breakers, rank filter, grouping, and final ordering are fixed; there are no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent schedules.
setup: CREATE TABLE service_tickets (ticket_id INT PRIMARY KEY, queue_name VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL, duration_minutes INT NOT NULL)

steps.sql: WITH ranked_durations AS (SELECT queue_name, ticket_id, duration_minutes, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY queue_name ORDER BY duration_minutes ASC, ticket_id ASC) AS ascending_rank, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY queue_name ORDER BY duration_minutes DESC, ticket_id DESC) AS descending_rank FROM service_tickets), median_by_queue AS (SELECT queue_name, AVG(duration_minutes) AS median_minutes FROM ranked_durations WHERE ABS(ascending_rank - descending_rank) <= 1 GROUP BY queue_name) SELECT queue_name, median_minutes FROM median_by_queue ORDER BY queue_name

checks.sql: SELECT queue_name, ticket_id, duration_minutes FROM service_tickets ORDER BY queue_name, duration_minutes, ticket_id
